jurisdiction.name: Saudi Arabia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Saudi Arabia's approach to AI governance combines guidance led by the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) with a small set of binding texts. The Copyright Law, in force since 12 August 2026, is the binding text identified so far with an AI-specific provision: Article 26(4) allows lawfully obtained works to be copied without permission to develop AI products and algorithms, and Article 30 of its Implementing Regulations sets conditions for that use. The Personal Data Protection Law, in force since September 2023, its Implementing Regulation and the data-transfer regulation govern personal data used in AI, including explicit consent and impact assessments for decisions based on automated processing. SDAIA leads the National Strategy for Data and AI (2020) and reports 13 regulatory instruments on AI, including ethics principles, generative AI guidelines, deepfake principles, AI market regulation tools and academic and occupational frameworks. The Council of Ministers designated 2026 the Year of Artificial Intelligence on 10 March 2026, and Riyadh hosted UNESCO's 4th Global Forum on the Ethics of AI from 14 to 17 September 2026, co-hosted by SDAIA and the International Center for AI Research and Ethics (ICAIRE), a UNESCO Category 2 centre. Sector bodies add their own rules, including the National Cybersecurity Authority, the Saudi Food and Drug Authority and the Communications, Space and Technology Commission.
lead_institutions: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
narrative.review_notes: SDAIA, the Umm Al-Qura official gazette, the national consultation platform and the cybersecurity, standards, intellectual property and food and drug authorities were searched, together with the ministries' own sites. A list of the national AI standards adopted in 2026 and some education and judicial AI guidance are listed under Leads until official documents are available.

instruments.current_status: Version 1.0, issued 22/9/1447H (11 March 2026). Binding on all Board of Grievances staff who use AI systems; compliance is monitored by its governance, risk and compliance directorate, and the document is reviewed annually.
instruments.scope: Board of Grievances (administrative judiciary) staff and contractors
instruments.summary: Covers building, developing and using AI at the Board of Grievances and its contractors. Seven principles: integrity and fairness; reliability and safety; transparency and explainability; accountability; privacy and security; humanity; social and environmental benefits. Excludes data classified "restricted" or higher; use needs data office approval and logging. Developers assess bias, enable human intervention and explain significant decisions; users avoid comprehensive personal profiling, watermark generative AI content and offer human alternatives. Roles: AI office, IT, cybersecurity, data office, HR, compliance. Cites SDAIA's AI Ethics Principles, government GenAI principles, AI Adoption Framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Internal AI rules of Saudi Arabia's administrative judiciary, binding on its staff.
instruments.evidence_reference: Details confirmed by Faisal, 2026-10-18, from the official PDF on bog.gov.sa. Version 1.0, dated 22/9/1447H (11 March 2026); approved by the President of the Board of Grievances and Chair of the Administrative Judicial Council; takes effect from its approval date. instruments.publisher_name: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Current edition dated May 2025 (document SDAIA-P114E, version 1, classified by SDAIA as a regulatory document); first published as version 1.0 in September 2023. SDAIA states that adopting entities are required to comply and that it monitors compliance directly or through sector regulators; registration is optional.
instruments.summary: Seven principles: fairness; privacy and security; humanity; social and environmental benefits; reliability and safety; transparency and explainability; and accountability and responsibility. They apply to all AI stakeholders in the Kingdom across the AI system lifecycle. Four risk levels: little or no risk; limited; high, with conformity assessments before and after deployment; and unacceptable, not allowed (for example social profiling or exploitation of children). Entity roles: head of entity or CDO, compliance officer, Responsible AI Officer and AI system assessor. Optional registration brings motivational badges and an assessment checklist.

instruments.summary: Ministry of Education guidebook, prepared with SDAIA, on the use of generative AI tools in Saudi general (school) education, addressed to students, teachers and parents. It explains how generative AI works and its benefits and risks, then sets usage rules: students under 13 should not use generative AI tools and those aged 13-18 need parental consent; AI-generated content used in assignments must be disclosed and cited, and non-disclosure is treated as academic dishonesty; outputs must be checked for bias and errors. A third part covers prompt-writing principles.

instruments.english_title: Copyright Law
instruments.issuing_authority: Council of Ministers; Royal Decree M/169
instruments.publisher_name: Council of Ministers; Royal Decree M/169
instruments.current_status: In force since 12 August 2026: under Article 61 it applies 180 days after its publication in the Umm Al-Qura gazette on 13 February 2026. Under Article 59 it replaces the Copyright Protection Law issued by Royal Decree M/41 of 2/7/1424H.
instruments.summary: Copyright law that replaces the 1424H Copyright Protection Law and is administered by the Saudi Authority for Intellectual Property. Article 26(4) allows the original of a work to be copied without the author's permission and without compensation "for the purposes of developing artificial intelligence products and algorithms", provided the work was lawfully published, the original copy was lawfully obtained and the copying stays within what the purpose requires.
instruments.evidence_reference: Full text (Articles 1-61) read on the Umm Al-Qura gazette page dated 1447-8-25 (13-02-2026). Royal Decree M/169: uqn.gov.sa/decisions-and-regulations/4000304; Council of Ministers Decision 560 approving the draft: /4000303. Effective date computed from Article 61 (180 days after publication). Article 26(4): "نسخ المصنَّف الأصلي لأغراض تطوير منتجات وخوارزميات الذكاء الاصطناعي بشرط أن يكون المصنَّف قد نشر بصورة مشروعة، وأن يكون الحصول على ملكية النسخة الأصلية بشكل مشروع، وأن يكون النسخ في حدود ما يلبي الغرض.". Issued by Royal Decree M/169 of 14/8/1447H after Council of Ministers Decision No. 560 of 8/8/1447H; administered by the Saudi Authority for Intellectual Property (SAIP). Published in the Umm Al-Qura gazette.

instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Authority for Intellectual Property, Board of Directors
instruments.publisher_name: Saudi Authority for Intellectual Property, Board of Directors
instruments.current_status: In force from 12 August 2026, the date the Copyright Law took effect (item 4 of the approval decision); published in the Umm Al-Qura gazette on 31 July 2026.
instruments.summary: Implementing regulations of the Copyright Law, adopted by the SAIP Board of Directors. Article 30 (Chapter 7, computer programs and uses of AI) sets conditions for copying works to develop AI products and algorithms under Article 26(4) of the Law: copying and analysis are limited to what the development requires, purely commercial use is excluded unless it is insubstantial, and developers must keep records of each work's type, source, purpose and date of use. Modifying, republishing or unnecessarily embedding the works in final products requires the right holder's permission.
instruments.evidence_reference: Full text (Articles 1-98) read on the Umm Al-Qura gazette page dated 1448-2-17 (31-07-2026); approval decision 33/ت/2026 at uqn.gov.sa/decisions-and-regulations/4001497 (document 01-1665-IPL-R-SAIP). Effective date from item 4 of the decision and Article 60 of the Law. Adopted by SAIP Board of Directors Decision No. 33/ت/2026 of 5/2/1448H. Published in the Umm Al-Qura gazette.

instruments.summary: SDAIA's implementing regulation of the Personal Data Protection Law, covering data-subject rights, consent, legitimate interest, disclosure, security, breach notification, impact assessments, data protection officers and records of processing. Controllers must tell data subjects whether decisions will be based wholly on automated processing (Art. 4), such decisions require explicit consent (Art. 11), and an impact assessment is required for decisions based on automated processing (Art. 25).

instruments.summary: SDAIA regulation setting the conditions for transferring or disclosing personal data to entities outside Saudi Arabia under the Personal Data Protection Law. It sets the permitted purposes, provides for a list of countries with an adequate level of protection, and requires standard contractual clauses, binding common rules or an accreditation certificate where an exemption is used, together with a transfer risk assessment.

instruments.official_title: سياسة الذكاء الاصطناعي المسؤول
instruments.english_title: Draft Responsible AI Policy
instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Draft published by SDAIA for public comment on Istitlaa, the national public consultation platform (page last updated 29 March 2026). The consultation ran from 3 April 2026 to 7 June 2026 and is marked finished. The final policy has not been published.
instruments.summary: SDAIA draft policy setting rules for the responsible development and use of AI systems in the Kingdom. It restates SDAIA's seven AI ethics principles as obligations for developers, operators and users, gives SDAIA oversight of AI systems under a national risk framework with critical, high, limited and minimal risk levels (critical-risk systems may not be released; high-risk systems need continuous monitoring, regular safety reports, human oversight and annual third-party audits), and requires a named person responsible for each AI agent. It also sets up an AI regulatory sandbox whose pass certificate high-risk system developers would need before entering the market. It is a consultation draft with no binding effect.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: SDAIA, the communications, cybersecurity, financial, standards and food and drug authorities, the national consultation platform and the official gazette were searched. No AI-specific procurement rules, AI regulatory sandbox or AI treaty ratification were found; this does not prove that none exist.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Searched SDAIA, CST, NCA, SAMA, SFDA, SASO, Istitlaa and the Bureau of Experts; no AI-specific procurement rules, AI regulatory sandbox, or AI treaty ratification located. "Not found" does not prove absence. Technical review notes: Pilot deep review. sdaia.gov.sa and laws.boe.gov.sa block automated access; dates verified through the Saudi Press Agency, Istitlaa, NCA, SASO and SFDA. Not recorded (out of category scope): National Occupational Standards Framework for Data & AI; Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications. Leads awaiting an official document: AI Principles in Media (Ministry of Media with SDAIA, 2026). Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 5 record(s) added. Ministries: Ministry of Education (schools): Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI in General Education, with SDAIA, 2025-01-24 (recorded); Education / National eLearning Center: AI-Supported Teaching and Learning Design Framework 2026-09, AI and Digital Education roadmap 2025, AI competencies 2025 (recorded); GenAI controls in digital education and prompt-engineering guide (leads, no stated date); Higher education / research: no separate Ministry of Education AI document found (Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications is SDAIA-hosted, not a ministry document); Ministry of Health: nothing AI-specific found (only data governance and open-data policies of the Sectorial Health AI & Data Management Office); Ministry of Justice / Supreme Judicial Council / Public Prosecution: nothing found; Board of Grievances: Principles for the Use of AI Systems (lead; site unreachable, no date read); Ministry of Defense: nothing found; Ministry of Finance / ZATCA: nothing found (ZATCA website disclaimer on AI-generated content only); Ministry of Interior: nothing found; Ministry of Foreign Affairs: no own AI document (US-Saudi Strategic AI Partnership, Nov 2025, is international; see needs_review); Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (labour, civil service): nothing found (news only); Ministry of Media: AI Principles in Media 2026 (recorded; promoted from lead); Ministry of Islamic Affairs: Friday-sermon directive on AI use only (not an instrument); Ministries of Hajj, Culture, Commerce, Tourism, Transport, Energy, Environment, Industry, Municipalities, Economy, Investment, MCIT: nothing found in site-restricted searches; Digital Government Authority (public administration): no AI-specific document found. Not reached: Board of Grievances site (bog.gov.sa) refused connections; Ministry of Media site (media.gov.sa) refused connections; other ministries checked by search only, not by browsing each site. Could not verify: Board of Grievances AI principles: bog.gov.sa unreachable by curl (connection reset) and WebFetch (503).; AI Principles in Media: exact launch date (February 2026 at the Saudi Media Forum per news) not found on an official page; year only recorded.; Ministry of Education guide PDF has no extractable text; content verified from rendered pages and the ministry's news page..

Method note (original): Pilot deep review. The websites of the Saudi Data and AI Authority and the Bureau of Experts' legal portal could not be read automatically; dates were checked against official announcements, the national consultation platform and the cybersecurity, standards and food and drug authorities. Occupational standards and an academic qualifications framework for AI were reviewed and not recorded. AI principles for the media sector (2026) are pending until an official document is published.

Deep review update 2026-10-17: Copyright Law and Implementing Regulations (uqn.gov.sa 4000299, 4001498), PDPL Implementing Regulation and transfer regulation (uqn.gov.sa p=23595, p=25412) and the Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications added; laws.boe.gov.sa and istitlaa.ncc.gov.sa did not respond; the reported list of 23 national AI standards (October 2026) has no official publication yet; SDAIA's Year of AI page reports 13 regulatory instruments on AI (press reports of 10 documents not used). Update 2026-10-18 (details confirmed by Faisal): Board of Grievances Principles for the Use of AI Systems (v1.0, 2026-03-11) promoted from lead to record; Generative AI Guidelines for Government Entities dated 2024-01 from the references listed in that document. Local retry 2026-10-18: Istitlaa (istitlaa.ncc.gov.sa, now redirecting to istitlaa.scbc.gov.sa) opened with curl from a Saudi connection; the AI-First Policy, Responsible AI Policy (path NDMO/ResponsibleAIPolicy) and Global AI Hub Law pages were read. The SDAIA project listing on Istitlaa loads by script and showed no items; the SharePoint API is not public. Local retry 2026-10-18 (SDAIA records): sdaia.gov.sa opened with curl from a Saudi connection (HTTP 200); the Arabic PDFs of the National AI Risk Management Framework, the four data and AI standards frameworks, the AI Market Regulation Tools, Generative AI Principles for the Public, Deepfakes guidelines, National AI Index and AI Bias Reference Guide (and English versions of the last four plus Market Regulation Tools) were downloaded and read; uqn.gov.sa decision 4001600 (ICAIRE statute approval) opened and was read.

Catch-up sweep 2026-10-19 (c1): checked sdaia.gov.sa Regulations and Policies page (curl, HTTP 200; AI items unchanged: ethics principles, professional standards framework, AI qualifications framework, GenAI principles for government and public, deepfakes, AI adoption framework), SDAIA news page (items load by script, list not readable; NewsByYear data source returned no items), istitlaa.scbc.gov.sa (project list loads by script; ResponsibleAIPolicy and globalailaw pages read in headless browser), plus web searches for NCA, SAMA, CMA, SFDA, MoE, NeLC, CST, uqn.gov.sa and laws.boe.gov.sa items since 2026-10-18. Found: Draft Responsible AI Policy consultation window 03/04/2026-07/06/2026, status finished (i-5f3c9e21ab74 -> consultation_closed); Draft Global AI Hub Law consultation window 14/04/2025-14/05/2025, status finished (i-sau-aihub-draft -> consultation_closed); new lead SDAIA Prompt Engineering Guide for Developers (April 2026, older, missing; PDF read, 42 pages). Ruled out: 'SDAIA AI companion device guidelines (February 2026)' - not found in official sources (checked: sdaia.gov.sa Regulations and Policies page and its document links, SDAIA news page, istitlaa.scbc.gov.sa, Arabic and English web searches); no SDAIA document on AI companions or companion devices was located. Not reached: SDAIA news list and Istitlaa project list (script-rendered); laws.boe.gov.sa not retried. Aggregator mention of a 2024 SDAIA 'Generative AI in Entertainment' guideline not verified (not on the Regulations and Policies page). Link check 2026-10-20 (i-sau-nca-ai-cyber), confirmed by Faisal in a regular browser: the consultation page now redirects to NCA's Public Consultations list, which shows 'AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' as Closed with no detail page; no final version on NCA's regulatory documents page. Original source_url kept as the official consultation URL; final 'AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (AICG-1:2026)' on the daily watch list.

leads.english_title: Approval of the founding statute of the International Center for AI Research and Ethics (ICAIRE)
leads.note: Umm Al-Qura gazette entry dated 14 August 2026 (uqn.gov.sa/decisions-and-regulations/4001600). Checked 2026-10-18: the page carries Council of Ministers Resolution No. (200) of 21/02/1448H, which approves the founding statute of the International Center for AI Research and Ethics "in the attached form" and authorises the chair of the Center's board to run its ordinary business until the board is formed, under the tripartite agreement with UNESCO (approved by Royal Decree M/116 of 21/6/1446H) that makes the Center a UNESCO category 2 centre. The text of the statute itself is not on the page.
